* 1. -main
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/-main
:FILE: src/graphden/executor_runtime/core.clj
:LINE: 187
:MINS: 1.2

 *Where the JVM starts.* Four lines that say what a graphden process IS: boot the Integrant system, install a shutdown hook, optionally open an nREPL (~GRAPHDEN_NREPL_PORT~ — the door the ~clojure~ MCP tools come through), then park forever. Nothing here serves HTTP; the web server is a ~:service~ row the reconciler starts, several components down.

* 2. boot!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/boot!
:FILE: src/graphden/executor_runtime/core.clj
:LINE: 167
:MINS: 2.0
:END:

Start, or HALT the partial system and exit non-zero. Integrant does NOT auto-halt when an init-key throws, and several components have already spawned non-daemon threads by then — without this the JVM stays half-alive with no shutdown hook and ~/health~ can pass on a boot that actually failed. The partial system rides in the ex-info's ~:system~ key. Read the docstring: it is the incident this function exists for.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/executor_runtime/core.clj::(defn boot!][src/graphden/executor_runtime/core.clj:167]]

* 3. read-config
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/read-config
:FILE: src/graphden/system/config.clj
:LINE: 83
:MINS: 1.9
:END:

Configuration is data: Aero reads ~system-<profile>.edn~ (~:dev~ / ~:test~ / ~:prod~) with ~#ig/ref~ and ~#var~ reader tags registered above, then deep-merges any ADDON config fragments named in ~GRAPHDEN_ADDON_CONFIGS~. That merge is the open-core seam (docs/TENANCY_SEAM.md § Addon config manifest) — the private tenancy addon REDEFINES core keys and ADDS its own without a single edit to this repo. With no addons the merge is a no-op.

~(ig/init (read-config profile))~ — that is the whole system lifecycle. The component graph and its dependency edges are documented in ~graphden.system.core~'s docstring, which exists only to ~:require~ the seven ~init.*~ namespaces for their ~defmethod~ side effects, so every ~ig/init-key~ is registered before this call. The next four steps walk that graph in dependency order.

* 5. postgres
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/postgres
:FILE: src/graphden/system/init/storage.clj
:LINE: 102
:MINS: 1.3
:END:

The first component with a socket (~:db/schema~ before it is pure — it is the ~create-builder~ + ~extend-builder~ chain from the storage block): open the Postgres pool, run ~initialize-with-cleanup!~ against that schema, seed traits. Note ~:datasource-wrap~ — a ~DataSource → DataSource~ fn the tenancy addon supplies so every connection carries ~graphden.current_org~ for row-level security. Absent in core: a plain pool. ~:db/versioned~ wraps this one in the versioning decorator.

* 7. context
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/context
:FILE: src/graphden/system/init/exec.clj
:LINE: 125
:MINS: 7.7
:END:

Assembles the one ~ExecutionContext~ the whole process runs against, and it reads as a list of the seams core exposes: auth-provider, request-scope, execute-guard, vault client, notify-emitter, fleet forward-hop, and ~:compile-storage~ — the privileged org-agnostic handle ~rebuild!~ reads the graph STRUCTURE through, while data reads stay org-scoped. In single-tenant every one of these is the default and the ~cond->~ tail is a no-op.

Two lines with a ~50s cost: compile every fn in the graph into a closure BEFORE the first request. This is the eager half of the executor's compile-once story — after this key, ~registry~ in the hot path is a warm holder read, never a cold compile.

* 9. dispatch-first
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/dispatch-first
:FILE: src/graphden/system/route_collection.clj
:LINE: 89
:MINS: 1.2
:END:

The last boot-time seam. Optional subsystems (the ~registry~ package, ~/mcp~) and the tenancy addon each install a ~:router-or-nil~ Ring callable here under a distinct key; the core handler chain tries them in turn and falls through to the app router on ~nil~. With nothing installed the collection is ~{}~, this short-circuits, and single-tenant behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged — the shape every seam in this codebase aims for.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/system/route_collection.clj::(defn dispatch-first][src/graphden/system/route_collection.clj:89]]

* 10. check-router!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/check-router!
:FILE: src/graphden/system/api_url_drift.clj
:LINE: 236
:MINS: 1.3
:END:

A boot-time guard rather than a component: enumerate the router's paths, scan every editor JS module for ~/api/*~ string literals, and refuse to start if one names a route the router does not serve. This is why the frontend never hardcodes a path the backend can silently move — the coupling is checked once, at boot, on the real router.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/system/api_url_drift.clj::(defn check-router!][src/graphden/system/api_url_drift.clj:236]]

* 11. -main
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/-main~2
:FILE: src/graphden/cli.clj
:LINE: 304
:MINS: 1.9
:END:

The same jar has a second entry point. ~graphden.cli~ moves whole branches between INSTANCES over the export/import HTTP API — ~export~ / ~import~ / ~diff~, and ~push~ / ~pull~ against a hub — with nothing but a URL and a token. It is how a self-hosted graph reaches a cloud org and back, and the model for any other out-of-process tool: the API is the contract, not the DB.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/cli.clj::(defn -main][src/graphden/cli.clj:304]]

* 12. register-checkpoint-hooks!
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: boot/register-checkpoint-hooks!
:FILE: src/graphden/crac.clj
:LINE: 202
:MINS: 1.5
:END:

CRaC (checkpoint/restore) is the optional fast-start track (docs/FLEET_RFC.md): snapshot the warmed JVM, restore in milliseconds. The catch is that CRIU cannot snapshot a socket, so ~quiesce!~ drains the Hikari pool, closes the LISTEN and advisory-lock connections and the http-kit server — schedulers paused FIRST so no tick reopens one mid-checkpoint — and ~resume!~ undoes it. Inert on a plain JVM; ~development/crac/~ has the bake.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/crac.clj::(defn register-checkpoint-hooks!][src/graphden/crac.clj:202]]
